repo_interim: Every change, including work in progress, is pushed to branches and merged into main through pull requests in the public repository: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsufiles/pulls?q=is%3Apr
version_unique: Each release has a unique version identifier, e.g. 2.4.0-vn.1 and 2.4.1-vn.1: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsufiles/releases
version_semver: Versions use MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH plus a -vn.N revision suffix (e.g. 2.4.1-vn.1); from the next release the tsudev scheme vYY.M.DDNN (VERSIONING v3).
version_tags: Every release is tagged in git (v2.4.0-vn.1, v2.4.1-vn.1): https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsufiles/tags
release_notes_vulns: No vulnerability with a CVE (or other public identifier) has been fixed in any release so far. Security fixes would be listed in CHANGELOG.md and the GitHub release notes.
report_tracker: GitHub Issues with bug, feature and format request templates: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsufiles/issues
report_responses: The project is young (first public release 11/11/2026); the maintainer reads and answers every issue. No external bug report has gone unanswered.
enhancement_responses: Feature requests use the feature_request / format_request templates and are labeled and answered by the maintainer.
report_archive: GitHub Issues and Discussions are public and searchable: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsufiles/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_process: SECURITY.md describes how to report vulnerabilities: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsufiles/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsufiles/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response: No vulnerability report was received in the last 6 months. SECURITY.md commits to acknowledge within 3 working days and give a first assessment within 7 days.
build: dotnet build TsuFiles.slnx (SDK version pinned in global.json). Packaging scripts in build/; CI builds Windows, Linux and macOS.
build_common_tools: Standard .NET SDK (dotnet build/test/publish) and PowerShell for packaging.
build_floss_tools: The .NET SDK (MIT), Avalonia (MIT) and PowerShell (MIT) are FLOSS.
test: xUnit test suites in tests/ (Core, Cli, App, Engines, Platform, Setup) are published with the source: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsufiles/tree/main/tests
test_invocation: Standard invocation: dotnet test TsuFiles.slnx (documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md).
test_most: Tests cover converters (real conversions), update download and signature verification, CLI, headless UI rendering of every page and the installer.
test_continuous_integration: GitHub Actions runs the full test suites on every push and pull request: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsufiles/actions/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy: CONTRIBUTING.md, Pull requests: 'make your change with tests'; the PR template asks how the change was tested: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsufiles/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
tests_are_added: Recent changes add tests with the code, e.g. PRs #57-#62 (data folder migration, command rename, bundle ids) and #79 (UI rendering test).
tests_documented_added: CONTRIBUTING.md and .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md require tests for changes.
warnings: C# compiler warnings with nullable reference types enabled (Directory.Build.props), .NET analyzers, and dotnet format --verify-no-changes --severity warn in CI.
warnings_fixed: CI fails on formatting and analyzer findings at warning severity, so warnings are fixed before merge.
warnings_strict: Nullable analysis is enabled for all projects and the format/analyzer gate runs at warning severity.
know_secure_design: The maintainer documented the threat model and defence layers (untrusted file parsing, isolation of external engines, signed updates): https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsufiles/blob/main/docs/vi/KIEN-TRUC-BAO-MAT.md
know_common_errors: The same document covers the common errors for this kind of software (path traversal / zip slip, network access during conversion, denial of service by crafted files, update tampering) and their mitigations.
crypto_published: Only published algorithms: ECDSA P-256 and SHA-256 via .NET System.Security.Cryptography.
crypto_call: No cryptographic primitives are implemented in the project; it calls the platform cryptography APIs.
crypto_floss: Cryptography comes from the .NET runtime (MIT) and the operating system.
crypto_keylength: Update signatures use ECDSA P-256 (128-bit security), hashes use SHA-256.
crypto_working: No broken algorithms are used for security. MD5 appears only as an ffprobe data-hash option for media info display, not for security.
crypto_weaknesses: No SHA-1 or MD5 for security decisions; signatures use ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256.
crypto_pfs: The software does not implement a network protocol; HTTPS is handled by the operating system/.NET HttpClient.
crypto_password_storage: The software has no user accounts and stores no passwords.
crypto_random: Keys are generated with ECDsa.Create (cryptographically secure RNG); no security-sensitive randomness uses System.Random.
delivery_unsigned: Hashes are never fetched over HTTP; the updater downloads SHA256SUMS over HTTPS and verifies its ECDSA signature before trusting any hash. Releases also carry GitHub build provenance attestations.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days: There are no known unpatched vulnerabilities (no open Dependabot or secret-scanning alerts).
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed: No critical vulnerability has been reported; dependency alerts are fixed through Dependabot PRs.
no_leaked_credentials: No credentials in the repository: gitleaks runs in CI, GitHub secret scanning and push protection are enabled, and the update signing key is kept offline (docs/vi/PHAT-HANH.md).
static_analysis: CodeQL (security-extended) on every push and pull request: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsufiles/blob/main/.github/workflows/security.yml, plus OpenSSF Scorecard.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities: CodeQL security-extended queries look for common C# vulnerabilities (injection, path traversal, unsafe deserialization, etc.).
static_analysis_fixed: No exploitable medium or higher finding is open. The only open CodeQL results (cs/cleartext-storage in Program.cs) are false positives: they log version, path, install kind and elevation level, no secrets.
static_analysis_often: CodeQL runs on every push and pull request and weekly.
dynamic_analysis: Weekly fuzzing of the in-house file format readers: https://github.com/tsudev-org/tsufiles/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml (tests/TsuFiles.Engines.Tests/ForkFuzzTests.cs).
dynamic_analysis_unsafe: Most code is memory-safe C#. The small Windows Explorer context-menu extension (src/Filee.ExplorerMenu/FileeExplorerMenu.c) is C and is not yet run under a memory-safety tool such as AddressSanitizer.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions: Tests and fuzzing run Debug/Release test builds with assertions (xUnit Assert, Debug.Assert in Debug) and --blame-crash.
dynamic_analysis_fixed: No exploitable medium or higher vulnerability has been found by fuzzing; findings would be fixed and turned into regression tests.
